# 1B.6 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** I found **moderate positive evidence** that Scholz resisted proliferation in the sense of supporting arms-control, nonproliferation, and de-escalatory multilateral language, while keeping Germany aligned with NATO deterrence. I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that he encouraged proliferation for short-term political gain. The main limitation is that the record is mostly rhetorical and alliance-based, not a concrete case of blocking a would-be proliferator.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **The Federal Chancellor’s 2024 summer press conference “I look forward to your questions”** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said long-range U.S. weapons were being stationed in Germany to protect Germany and NATO states and to prevent war, and added that Russia had massively violated past arms-control agreements while “we all wish to live in a world where arms control plays an important role again.” This is the clearest 1B.6 evidence: he frames security policy as compatible with arms control, not as a substitute for it. | 1B.6, 1B.4, 1B.1 |
| **Speech by Olaf Scholz at "Summit of the Future Global Call"** | Federal Government | 12 Sep 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-chancellor-summit-of-the-future-global-call-2308462 | Scholz explicitly said nuclear proliferation poses growing threats and framed the international order in terms of peace, stability, and multilateral repair. This is strong evidence of nonproliferation-minded good faith. | 1B.6, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| **Speech by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany at the reception on the occasion of the Summit of the Future** | Federal Government | 23 Sep 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-by-olaf-scholz-chancellor-of-the-federal-republic-of-germany-at-the-reception-on-the-occasion-of-the-summit-of-the-future-new-york-23-september-2024-2310980 | Scholz celebrated renewed commitment to the UN Charter, international law, and institutional reform of the international system. This is indirect but relevant evidence that he backed de-escalatory multilateral structures rather than proliferation incentives. | 1B.6, 1B.4 |
| **Federal Chancellor Scholz’ press conference at the NATO Summit** | Federal Government | 11 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/pc-chancellor-nato-summit-2298906 | Scholz emphasized NATO deterrence and alliance security rather than arms-control diplomacy. This is the main borderline counterweight: it shows priority on deterrence, but not support for proliferation. | 1B.6, 1B.4 |
| **Scholz: Nichtbeteiligung deutscher Soldaten sicherstellen** | Deutscher Bundestag | 13 Mar 2024 | https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw11-de-regierungsbefragung-991060 | Scholz said he would not approve long-range systems if German soldiers had to be involved outside Ukraine, because he wanted to ensure no German participation in the war. This is relevant because it resists operational entanglement that could normalize broader proliferation or escalation pressures. | 1B.6, 1B.5, 1B.1 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that Scholz resisted a specific allied, proxy, or domestic proliferation push in a concrete negotiation.
- I also did **not** find evidence that he used proliferation arguments opportunistically for short-term political gain.
- The available record is mostly **principled rhetoric**: support for arms control, warnings about proliferation, and a preference for multilateral institutions, alongside continued NATO deterrence.

## Synthesis for 1B.6

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz acted in line with resisting proliferation, especially through explicit support for arms control and nonproliferation language in 2024.
- **Confidence:** moderate, because the evidence is clear on his stated posture but thin on a direct case of resisting a proliferator.
- **Main caveat:** his 2024 security policy leaned heavily on NATO deterrence, so this is not an anti-deterrence position. It is better read as pro-nonproliferation within an alliance framework.
